This is a better idea in my opinion than just banning submissions, or deleting them if they're not in the correct subverse.
Is it possible to send submissions to other subverses if the discussions are not appropriate for the subverse they're initially submitted too?

Well there are multiple possibilities to realize this idea:

  • When a mod bans a submission, the op gets the option to move the submission to another subverse.

  • An op gets a button/link next to save / source /... for "move" or "copy"

But both approaches have a problem: what about the comments? are they moved to? what if op is a "funny" guy and moves it to some "offensive" subverser for the users that commented until then?

It would be up to the mods to move the entire thread including comments. Once the OP makes the submission they no longer have control of the thread, that way there is no funny business with switching to a subverse to offend someone. It would be the mods job to, you know, moderate their subverse. This could actually create a very healthy relationship between subverses as mods become more familiar with each other and other subverses. They could send content to the proper place where more people would enjoy it or if it's more suitable for a certain subverse. I do think a notification to the OP would be a nice gesture letting them know the submission was moved.

Extract of an old photoalbum from the 30's

I bought a photoalbum from the 1930's, with the intent to giving it back to the still living relatives. I believe most of the pictures were taken in Germany.

What I do is analyze all of the pictures for clues on locations and people. Brand names, style of clothing, a bridge in the distance, a foto in a park or a memorial. They all give me small little details about the life of the person who took the picture.

I bought the album a couple of days ago and now know the family name and roughly where they lived. I will be searching for living relatives soon and trying to get in contact with them.

It's a pretty cool search and really makes you use your brain.

Over at /v/helpmefind we are collectively looking for clues now.

Thank god you blacked out their faces. We may just recognized the adults pictured in these photographs from the 1930's.... /s

Very interesting though. My local town publishes photos from their archives every now and then and I love going through and looking at photos of random places in America during the 'old days'. It's always very interesting to see how landscapes and towns have changed over time.

The reason I blacked out the faces is to protect the privacy of any living relatives. Although i bought the album, and it's technically my property, i do not feel comfortable posting recognizable pictures.

Deceased people don't have privacy, but I'd like the approval of the family before disclosing the whole album. I'm just trying to do the right thing.
